claim: SETD2 is the only known enzyme that catalyzes H3K36me3 in human somatic cells.
source: In humans, SETD2 is the only known enzyme that catalyzes H3K36me3 in somatic cells and is implicated in tumor suppression across multiple cancer types.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Edmunds et al., 2008).

claim: Setd2 functions as a potent tumor suppressor in a KRASG12C-driven lung adenocarcinoma mouse model.
source: Here, we show that Setd2 functions as a potent tumor suppressor in a KRASG12C-driven lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) mouse model, and that acetylation enhances SETD2 in vitro methylation of H3K36 on nucleosome substrates.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the in vivo mouse model experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Acetylation enhances SETD2 in vitro methylation of H3K36 on nucleosome substrates.
source: Here, we show that Setd2 functions as a potent tumor suppressor in a KRASG12C-driven lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) mouse model, and that acetylation enhances SETD2 in vitro methylation of H3K36 on nucleosome substrates.
evidence: This claim is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Setd2 ablation accelerates lethality in an autochthonous KRASG12C-driven LUAD mouse tumor model.
source: In vivo, Setd2 ablation accelerates lethality in an autochthonous KRASG12C-driven LUAD mouse tumor model.
evidence: This is supported by survival data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Polyacetylation of histone tails in a nucleosome context promotes H3K36 methylation by SETD2.
source: Biochemical analyses reveal that polyacetylation of histone tails in a nucleosome context promotes H3K36 methylation by SETD2.
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: Monoacetylation exerts position-specific effects to stimulate SETD2 methylation activity.
source: In addition, monoacetylation exerts position-specific effects to stimulate SETD2 methylation activity.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4B and 4C showing differential effects of acetylation at different positions.

claim: Mono-ubiquitination at various histone sites, including at H2AK119 and H2BK120, does not affect SETD2 methylation of nucleosomes.
source: In contrast, mono-ubiquitination at various histone sites, including at H2AK119 and H2BK120, does not affect SETD2 methylation of nucleosomes.
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data shown in Figure 5B, 5C, and 5D.

claim: Protein lysine methylation occurs in three distinct states: monomethylation (Kme1), dimethylation (Kme2), and trimethylation (Kme3).
source: Protein lysine methylation is a common post-translational modification (PTM) that occurs in three distinct states—monomethylation (Kme1), dimethylation (Kme2), and trimethylation (Kme3)—depending on whether one, two, or three methyl groups are added to the lysine side chain (Bhat et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Bhat et al., 2021.

claim: Lysine methylation is catalyzed by protein lysine methyltransferases (KMTs) and removed by protein lysine demethylases.
source: Lysine methylation is catalyzed by a class of enzymes named protein lysine methyltransferases (KMTs) and removed by protein lysine demethylases (Bhat et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Bhat et al., 2021.

claim: Methylation at H3K36 is an evolutionarily conserved histone modification.
source: Methylation at H3K36 is an evolutionarily conserved histone modification (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: Mutations in enzymes that determine H3K36 methylation dynamics are linked to developmental disorders and cancer in humans.
source: In humans, mutations in the enzymes that determine H3K36 methylation dynamics are linked to a variety of developmental disorders and cancer (Li et al., 2019; Husmann and Gozani, 2019; Bennett et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019; Husmann and Gozani, 2019; Bennett et al., 2017.

claim: H3K36me2 is generated by four related enzymes: NSD1, NSD2, NSD3, and ASH1L.
source: The state and extent of methylation at H3K36 are synthesized by distinct KMTs, with H3K36me2 generated by four related enzymes (NSD1, NSD2, NSD3, and ASH1L), whereas SETD2 is the only human enzyme in somatic cells that has been reproducibly shown to generate H3K36me3 (Li et al., 2019; Husmann and Gozani, 2019; Edmunds et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Li et al., 2019; Husmann and Gozani, 2019.

claim: SETD2 and H3K36me3 generally occupy transcriptionally active regions.
source: SETD2 and its cognate mark H3K36me3 generally occupy transcriptionally active regions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: SETD2 influences DNA methylation, RNA processing, DNA repair, and genomic integrity.
source: Functionally, SETD2 influences core molecular processes such as DNA methylation, RNA processing, DNA repair, and genomic integrity (Baubec et al., 2015; Jha et al., 2014; de Almeida et al., 2011; Duns et al., 2010; Zhu et al., 2014; Wen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations: Baubec et al., 2015; Jha et al., 2014; de Almeida et al., 2011; Duns et al., 2010; Zhu et al., 2014; Wen et al., 2014.

claim: H3K36me2-generating enzymes like NSD2 and NSD3 promote oncogenesis when mutated or overexpressed.
source: Notably, while H3K36me2-generating enzymes like NSD2 and NSD3 promote oncogenesis when mutated or overexpressed (e.g., Kuo et al., 2011; Hudlebusch et al., 2011; Jaffe et al., 2013; Aytes et al., 2018; Yuan et al., 2021; Sengupta et al., 2021), SETD2 is a potent tumor suppressor frequently mutated in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) (Duns et al., 2010; Dalgliesh et al., 2010) and several other cancers.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations: Kuo et al., 2011; Hudlebusch et al., 2011; Jaffe et al., 2013; Aytes et al., 2018; Yuan et al., 2021; Sengupta et al., 2021.

claim: SETD2 is a potent tumor suppressor frequently mutated in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC).
source: Notably, while H3K36me2-generating enzymes like NSD2 and NSD3 promote oncogenesis when mutated or overexpressed (e.g., Kuo et al., 2011; Hudlebusch et al., 2011; Jaffe et al., 2013; Aytes et al., 2018; Yuan et al., 2021; Sengupta et al., 2021), SETD2 is a potent tumor suppressor frequently mutated in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) (Duns et al., 2010; Dalgliesh et al., 2010) and several other cancers.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Duns et al., 2010; Dalgliesh et al., 2010.

claim: The SETD2 gene is located within chromosome 3p, a genomic region showing loss of heterozygosity in ~90–95% of ccRCC tumors.
source: For example, the SETD2 gene (along with other important tumor suppressors) is located within chromosome 3p, a genomic region that is reported to show loss of heterozygosity in ~90–95% of ccRCC tumors (Walton et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Walton et al., 2023.

claim: In ccRCC pathogenesis, ~10–20% of tumors acquire SETD2 mutation on the second intact allele, resulting in biallelic loss of SETD2 and H3K36me3 depletion.
source: In ccRCC pathogenesis, ~10–20% of tumors acquire SETD2 mutation on the second intact allele (or more rarely acquire mutations on both alleles), resulting in biallelic loss of SETD2 and H3K36me3 depletion (Duns et al., 2010; Dalgliesh et al., 2010; Walton et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Duns et al., 2010; Dalgliesh et al., 2010; Walton et al., 2023.

claim: Deletions and/or loss-of-function mutations in SETD2 are detected recurrently in different types of leukemia and solid tumors, including gastroesophageal cancers and lung adenocarcinoma.
source: Deletions and/or loss-of-function mutations in SETD2 are also detected recurrently in different types of leukemia and solid tumors, including gastroesophageal cancers and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), though at lower frequency than seen in ccRCC (Zhu et al., 2014; Foggetti et al., 2021; Kadara et al., 2017; Walter et al., 2017; Mar et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhu et al., 2014; Foggetti et al., 2021; Kadara et al., 2017; Walter et al., 2017; Mar et al., 2017.

claim: SETD2-catalyzed H3K36me3 allosterically inhibits the ability of the PRC2 complex to synthesize the repressive H3K27me3 chromatin modification.
source: One established function of SETD2-catalyzed H3K36me3 is to allosterically inhibit the ability of the PRC2 complex to synthesize the repressive H3K27me3 chromatin modification (Cookis et al., 2025; Yuan et al., 2011; Schmitges et al., 2011; Jani et al., 2019; Finogenova et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cookis et al., 2025; Yuan et al., 2011; Schmitges et al., 2011; Jani et al., 2019; Finogenova et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2022.

claim: H3K36me3, via its recognition by the PWWP domain of DNMT3b, promotes targeted DNA methylation.
source: Further, H3K36me3, via its recognition by the PWWP domain of DNMT3b, promotes targeted DNA methylation (Baubec et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Baubec et al., 2015.

claim: G12C is the most common KRAS mutation in lung adenocarcinoma.
source: Here, we test the in vivo role of SETD2 in suppressing KRASG12C-driven tumorigenesis in LUAD, as G12C is the most common KRAS mutation in this tumor type, and identify potential regulatory roles for histone acetylation, particularly H3K27 acetylation, in promoting in vitro methylation of nucleosomes by SETD2.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citations in the introduction (Campbell et al., 2016; Wiesweg et al., 2019).

claim: Previous in vivo studies demonstrated that loss of SETD2 promotes LUAD tumorigenesis in the canonical KRASG12D-driven LUAD mouse tumor model.
source: Several elegant previous in vivo studies utilizing either CRISPR-based or gene knockout approaches demonstrated that loss of SETD2 promotes LUAD tumorigenesis in the canonical KRASG12D-driven LUAD mouse tumor model (Walter et al., 2017; Johnson et al., 2001; Jackson et al., 2001; Rogers et al., 2018; Xie et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Walter et al., 2017; Johnson et al., 2001; Jackson et al., 2001; Rogers et al., 2018; Xie et al., 2023.

claim: Setd2 deletion results in loss of H3K36me3 in LUAD tissue.
source: Consistent with the principal catalytic activity of SETD2 being generation of H3K36me3, Setd2 deletion resulted in loss of H3K36me3 immunohistochemistry (IHC) signal comparing LUAD tissue sections from KcP and KcP;Setd2 mice (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Setd2 depletion causes a modest increase in tumor nodule numbers in the KRASG12C-driven LUAD model.
source: Moreover, Setd2 depletion accelerated tumorigenesis as measured by a modest increase in tumor nodule numbers and a fourfold increase in tumor burden (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Setd2 depletion causes a fourfold increase in tumor burden in the KRASG12C-driven LUAD model.
source: Moreover, Setd2 depletion accelerated tumorigenesis as measured by a modest increase in tumor nodule numbers and a fourfold increase in tumor burden (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Loss of Setd2 causes an increase in cellular proliferation in tumors.
source: Loss of Setd2 also caused an increase in cellular proliferation in tumors, but did not significantly impact apoptosis levels (Figure 1E, H, I).
evidence: This is supported by Ki67 IHC data shown in Figure 1E and quantification in Figure 1H.

claim: Loss of Setd2 does not significantly impact apoptosis levels in tumors.
source: Loss of Setd2 also caused an increase in cellular proliferation in tumors, but did not significantly impact apoptosis levels (Figure 1E, H, I).
evidence: This is supported by cleaved Caspase3 IHC data shown in Figure 1E and quantification in Figure 1I.

claim: Setd2 depletion results in a 40% decline in animal overall median survival time in the KRASG12C-driven LUAD model.
source: Finally, Setd2 depletion resulted in a 40% decline in animal overall median survival time (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is supported by survival data shown in Figure 1J (median survival 151 days for KcP vs 92 days for KcP;Setd2).

claim: The isolated catalytic SET domain of SETD2 methylates unmodified recombinant nucleosomes in vitro with the same efficiency as H3KC36me2 rNucs.
source: However, previous work demonstrated that the isolated catalytic SET domain of SETD2 methylates unmodified recombinant nucleosomes (rNucs) in vitro with the same efficiency as methyl-lysine analog (MLA)-based H3KC36me2 rNucs (Li et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2009.

claim: SETD2SET methylates all rNuc substrates except the tri-methylated sample.
source: The SETD2SET domain methylated all the rNuc substrates besides the tri-methylated sample (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by autoradiography data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: SETD2SET shows the highest methylation signal on unmodified rNucs, with signal intensity decreasing sequentially on H3K36me1 and H3K36me2 rNuc substrates.
source: Specifically, the highest signal was observed using unmodified rNucs, with the intensity of the signal decreasing sequentially on H3K36me1 and H3K36me2 rNuc substrates, likely reflecting the reduced capacity of these H3K36 methylated histones to be further methylated (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by autoradiography data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: SETD2SET shows no detectable methylation activity on H3K36me3 rNucs.
source: SETD2SET showed no detectable methylation activity on H3K36me3 rNucs, consistent with K36 being 100% saturated with methylation and thus there being no more sites available to be methylated and the specificity of SETD2 for K36 versus other lysine residues on histones (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by autoradiography data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: NSD2SET shows the strongest methylation activity on unmodified rNucs compared to H3K36me1 rNucs.
source: Like with SETD2SET, the NSD2SET domain showed the strongest methylation activity on unmodified rNucs compared to H3K36me1 rNucs, and NSD2SET has no activity on H3K36me2/3 rNucs, consistent with NSD2 being a selective H3K36me2-KMT (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by autoradiography data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: NSD2SET has no activity on H3K36me2/3 rNucs.
source: Like with SETD2SET, the NSD2SET domain showed the strongest methylation activity on unmodified rNucs compared to H3K36me1 rNucs, and NSD2SET has no activity on H3K36me2/3 rNucs, consistent with NSD2 being a selective H3K36me2-KMT (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by autoradiography data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: SETD2SET generates all three methyl states (me1, me2, and me3) when using unmodified rNucs as substrate.
source: Under our reaction conditions (see 'Materials and methods'), SETD2SET generated all three methyl states (me1, me2, and me3) when using unmodified rNucs as substrate (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: On H3K36me1-rNucs, SETD2SET generates both H3K36me2 and H3K36me3.
source: On H3K36me1-rNucs, SETD2SET generated both higher states of methylation at K36 (H3K36me2 and H3K36me3), whereas H3K36me2-rNucs were naturally only converted to the trimethyl state (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: H3K36me2-rNucs are converted only to the trimethyl state by SETD2SET.
source: On H3K36me1-rNucs, SETD2SET generated both higher states of methylation at K36 (H3K36me2 and H3K36me3), whereas H3K36me2-rNucs were naturally only converted to the trimethyl state (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The conversion to the trimethyl state at K36 is most efficient on H3K36me2-rNucs.
source: The conversion to the trimethyl state at K36 was most efficient on H3K36me2-rNucs, which likely reflects the reaction having poor in vitro processivity (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The ability of SETD2SET to generate H3K36me3 in vitro does not require pre-existing methylation.
source: These results indicate that the ability of SETD2SET to generate H3K36me3 in vitro does not require pre-existing methylation, consistent with previous studies (Li et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data in Figure 2 and citation to Li et al., 2009.

claim: SETD2SET is agnostic about the state of methylation at H3K36 on nucleosome substrates in vitro.
source: The data further suggests that, at least in vitro, SETD2SET is agnostic about the state of methylation at H3K36 on nucleosome substrates.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Histone acetylation promotes transcription through recognition of acetyl-lysine by reader proteins and neutralization of DNA-histone interactions.
source: Histone acetylation promotes transcription and other DNA-templated processes through several mechanisms, such as the recognition of acetyl-lysine by reader proteins and the neutralization of DNA-histone interactions (Nitsch et al., 2021; Ghoneim et al., 2021; Jain et al., 2023).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Nitsch et al., 2021; Ghoneim et al., 2021; Jain et al., 2023.

claim: Neutralizing the positive charge on the lysine side chain facilitates accessibility of KMTs to the unstructured histone tails by disrupting tail-DNA interactions.
source: In addition, neutralizing the positive charge on the lysine side chain facilitates accessibility of KMTs to the unstructured histone tails by disrupting tail-DNA interactions, as was previously shown for the MLL1 KMT complex (Ghoneim et al., 2021; Jain et al., 2023; Marunde et al., 2024; Fox et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ghoneim et al., 2021; Jain et al., 2023; Marunde et al., 2024; Fox et al., 2024.

claim: SETD2SET methylation activity is enhanced on tetra-acetylated rNucs compared to control rNucs irrespective of the acetylated histone tail.
source: SETD2SET methylation activity as determined by incorporation of radiolabeled SAM or SAH production was enhanced on tetra-acetylated rNucs compared to control rNucs irrespective of the acetylated histone tail (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by autoradiography and MTase-Glo assay data shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: H3 tetra-acetylation has the biggest impact on NSD2SET methylation activity compared to acetylation of H2A and H4.
source: A similar trend was observed in methylation assays using the NSD2SET domain, though H3 tetra-acetylation seemed to have the biggest impact compared to acetylation of H2A and H4 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by autoradiography data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Methylation assays using hDOT1L were not enhanced by acetylation of various histone tails.
source: In contrast, methylation assays using hDOT1L, the KMT responsible for H3K79 methylation—a PTM situated in the nucleosome globular domain—were not enhanced by acetylation of the various histone tails (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by autoradiography data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: A high degree of acetylation may increase the accessibility of H3K36 to the enzymes that methylate this residue.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that a high degree of acetylation may increase the accessibility of H3K36 to the enzymes that methylate this residue.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Three different single acetylation sites (K14, K23, and K27) enhance SETD2SET methylation activity on nucleosomes.
source: Methylation activity, determined by incorporation of radiolabeled SAM (Figure 4B) or SAH production (Figure 4C), indicated that three different single acetylation sites (K14, K23, and K27) enhanced SETD2SET methylation activity on nucleosomes, with the impact likely H3K27ac>H3K14ac>H3K23ac (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is supported by autoradiography and MTase-Glo assay data shown in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: The impact of single acetylation sites on SETD2SET methylation activity is likely H3K27ac>H3K14ac>H3K23ac.
source: Methylation activity, determined by incorporation of radiolabeled SAM (Figure 4B) or SAH production (Figure 4C), indicated that three different single acetylation sites (K14, K23, and K27) enhanced SETD2SET methylation activity on nucleosomes, with the impact likely H3K27ac>H3K14ac>H3K23ac (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is inferred from the quantitative data shown in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: SETD2SET is more efficiently pulled down when using H3K27ac rNucs as bait compared to unmodified rNucs.
source: Consistent with this, SETD2SET was subtly more efficiently pulled down when using H3K27ac rNucs as bait compared to unmodified rNucs and the ability of SETD2SET to form a complex with recombinant mono-nucleosomes was subtly enhanced in the presence of K27 acetylation (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is supported by nucleosome pulldown assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The ability of SETD2SET to form a complex with recombinant mono-nucleosomes is subtly enhanced in the presence of K27 acetylation.
source: Consistent with this, SETD2SET was subtly more efficiently pulled down when using H3K27ac rNucs as bait compared to unmodified rNucs and the ability of SETD2SET to form a complex with recombinant mono-nucleosomes was subtly enhanced in the presence of K27 acetylation (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: K27ac may directly or indirectly influence the interaction between SETD2SET and its substrate site in the context of nucleosomes.
source: These data suggest K27ac may directly or indirectly minorly influence the interaction between SETD2SET and its substrate site in the context of nucleosomes (see 'Discussion').
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 4D and 4E.

claim: H3K27me3 recruits the PRC1 complex, which catalyzes the ubiquitination of H2AK119.
source: Specifically, H3K27me3 recruits the PRC1 complex, which catalyzes the ubiquitination of H2AK119 (H2AK119ub) (de Napoles et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to de Napoles et al., 2004.

claim: Nucleosomes harboring H2AK119ub antagonize H3K36 enzymes like NSD2 by structurally preventing their proper association with the nucleosome.
source: Nucleosomes harboring H2AK119ub antagonize H3K36 enzymes like NSD2 by structurally preventing their proper association with the nucleosome (Li et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2021.

claim: Studies in yeast have shown the SETD2 homolog, Set2, is influenced by H2BK120ub.
source: However, whether H2AK119ub and/or other histone ubiquitination sites impact SETD2 activity is unclear, although studies in yeast have shown the SETD2 homolog, Set2, is influenced by H2BK120ub (Bilokapic and Halic, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bilokapic and Halic, 2019.

claim: Histone ubiquitination does not impact SETD2 activity.
source: Surprisingly, assaying methylation by three different methods (utilizing radiolabeled SAM, detecting the different methylation states by Western, and measuring SAH generation), histone ubiquitination did not impact SETD2 activity (Figure 5B–D; note that the H3K36me2 antibody is blocked by H3K14 and H3K18 ubiquitination).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5B, 5C, and 5D using three different assay methods.

claim: H2AK119ub specifically reduces NSD2 activity.
source: In contrast, as expected, H2AK119ub specifically reduced NSD2 activity (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by autoradiography data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The isolated catalytic domain of SETD2, unlike NSD2, is not influenced by histone ubiquitination.
source: Collectively, these findings indicate that the isolated catalytic domain of SETD2, unlike for NSD2, is not influenced by histone ubiquitination, suggesting potential functional differences in how H3K36 enzymes interact with the ubiquitinated nucleosome landscape.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: SETD2 mutations cause Sotos-like syndrome, an overgrowth disorder.
source: Mutations in SETD2 cause Sotos-like syndrome, an overgrowth disorder, and loss of SETD2 commonly occurs and is thought to be tumor suppressive in ccRCC and many other malignancies (Husmann and Gozani, 2019; Luscan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Husmann and Gozani, 2019; Luscan et al., 2014.

claim: SETD2 was identified as one of the most mutated genes in a saturation analysis of 21 cancer types.
source: Indeed, SETD2 was identified as one of the most mutated genes in a saturation analysis of 21 cancer types (Lawrence et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lawrence et al., 2014.

claim: Setd2 ablation strongly accelerates LUAD malignant progression and lethality in a KRASG12C-driven mouse tumor model.
source: Consistent with these observations and previous lung cancer mouse modeling studies (Walter et al., 2017; Rogers et al., 2018; Xie et al., 2023), we find that Setd2 ablation strongly accelerates LUAD malignant progression and lethality in a KRASG12C-driven mouse tumor model (see Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 1 and citations to previous studies.

claim: EZM0414, a clinical-grade SETD2 inhibitor, was being evaluated in a phase I clinical trial as a therapeutic in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma and diffuse large B cell lymphoma.
source: In this context, EZM0414, a clinical-grade SETD2 inhibitor, was being evaluated in a phase I clinical trial as a therapeutic in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma and diffuse large B cell lymphoma, suggesting that at least in these cancer types, H3K36me3 generation may be oncogenic (NCT05121103; note this trial was terminated).
evidence: This is stated as factual information with a clinical trial identifier.

claim: The catalytic domain of SETD2 does not exhibit a preference for substrates bearing mono- or di-methylation at K36 compared to the unmodified state.
source: Consistent with previous work, our biochemical analyses using native designer nucleosomes indicate that—at least in isolation—the catalytic domain of SETD2 does not exhibit a preference for substrates bearing mono- or di-methylation at K36 compared to the unmodified state (see Figure 2; Li et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 2 and citation to Li et al., 2009.

claim: Physiologically, SETD2 uses all three lower states of methylation at H3K36me (me0-me2) to generate endogenous H3K36me3.
source: We speculate that physiologically SETD2 uses all three lower states of methylation at H3K36me (me0-me2) to generate endogenous H3K36me3, with the specific precursor state determined by the underlying biology and genomic context.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the experimental data.

claim: Certain acetylation events may alter histone-DNA interactions in a manner that renders H3K36 more accessible to the catalytic pocket of SETD2.
source: One possibility is that certain acetylation events, for example, H3K27ac, may alter histone-DNA interactions in a manner that renders H3K36 more accessible to the catalytic pocket of SETD2.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning to explain the experimental observations.

claim: SETD2 may interact more strongly with H3K27ac nucleosomes compared to unmodified nucleosomes.
source: Additionally, our data suggests that SETD2 may interact more strongly with H3K27ac nucleosomes compared to unmodified nucleosomes, which would promote higher levels of methylation (Figure 4).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: SETD2 is neither inhibited by H2AK119ub nor regulated by H2BK120ub.
source: Finally, we observed a divergence between SETD2 and H3K36me2-KMTs such as NSD2, in that SETD2 is neither inhibited by H2AK119ub nor regulated by H2BK120ub (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Recent cryo-EM-based structural studies provide a molecular rationale for why NSD2, but not SETD2, would be impacted by a large modification within the C-terminal region of H2A.
source: These data are consistent with recent cryo-EM-based structural studies, which provide a molecular rationale for why NSD2, but not SETD2, would be impacted by a large modification within the C-terminal region of H2A (Li et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2021; Markert et al., 2025).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2021; Markert et al., 2025.

claim: KcP mutant mice develop widespread LUAD with 100% penetrance following Ad-Cre viral infection.
source: Following viral infection, KcP mutant mice develop widespread LUAD with 100% penetrance (see schematic, Figure 1D; Francis et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Francis et al., 2024 and the experimental design shown in Figure 1D.
